title: Prove on Pi 1.0 that typed context reaches a running worker and scope changes get one log-or-ask turn
action: Leader-run (the worker-outward guard refuses a worker that starts pi). In a fresh verify-app sandbox with the candidate vendored: (a) dispatch a no-pane Pi worker on a small cell, run bee herding steer on its job while it runs, and show the text in the worker's session; (b) type a scope-change follow-up to a Pi leader and show one forced turn asking to log it or ask the user; (c) show a worktree worker recording its verdict. Record the evidence in the feature file and the audit page.

truths: steered text appears in the running worker's session once
a typed scope change gets one forced log-or-ask turn and no gate approval
a worktree worker records its verdict
the feature file names the run id and evidence path

trace.outcome: Live Pi 1.0 proof: a steer reached a running worktree worker once (it declined a scope-changing steer by design), the worktree worker recorded its verdict, a late steer was refused, and a typed scope change got one forced turn while bee refused an unapproved cell add
deviations: leader-run instead of a worker — the worker-outward guard refuses a worker that starts pi — hit an unforeseen obstacle
the steer test text asked for a scope change, which the worker correctly declined; delivery is proven by the worker report quoting it — found a better route
in the scope run the small model answered the forced turn with an empty message; filed as a backlog finding — something else had to be fixed first
